coverage.notes: No framework is recorded for New Hampshire, so there are no items or alignments. SEL: the Department of Education's Office of Student and Educator Wellness page  describes MTSS-B (a multi-tiered behavioral health and wellness model), toolkits and training; the Department's 2020 back-to-school wellness page has an SEL section that defines SEL and promotes professional development. I found no K-12 SEL standards or competencies on education.nh.gov, and the Ed 306 minimum standards for school approval (adopted text dated December 12, 2024; I searched it for social, emotional, portrait and wellness terms and read the graduation-requirements section) contain none. Third-party summaries say NH has early learning standards that include social-emotional development; I did not open them, so they are not recorded. The education.nh.gov site is mid-redesign and many old pages return 'not found', so the absence of a standards page is not proof. PORTRAIT OF A GRADUATE: the Ed 306 text has no Portrait of a Graduate. Its graduation requirements (Ed 306 section on high school graduation) list 'all programs and courses' skills such as communicating effectively, thinking independently, contributing respectfully and persevering with self-reflection; these are state graduation requirements, not a named portrait, so they are not recorded as one. A June 3, 2024 Concord Monitor news report (secondary source, not a state document) says the nonprofit New Hampshire Learning Initiative drafted a portrait of a New Hampshire learner, that it is not part of Ed 306 or state graduation requirements, and that at least eight districts have written their own. REVIEWER: confirm district_led_only against education.nh.gov or the State Board of Education; if the Department has since issued a portrait, change the status and add the framework.
